one_month_reasoning: No Jabil earnings fall in the window; Q1 FY27 is due mid-December 2026. The FY26 print (Sep 30) is out: a ~3.7% guide beat over the $16.92 consensus, a -10.0% close-to-close drop (318.84 to 286.86), then +6% over two sessions to 304.41. Events inside the window: hyperscaler September-quarter results and 2027 capex commentary (about Oct 27-30). That is the main swing factor, because cloud/data center is $17.5B (+52%) of the FY27 guide. Consensus CY27 capex growth (~23%) has been too low two years running, so the asymmetry is mildly positive. The late-October FOMC and tariff headlines also fall in the window; I no longer weight the thin Polymarket rate and tariff markets. Post-earnings drift after a positive fundamental surprise, plus a partly retraced sell-the-news move, argue for a small upward tilt. The ladder is a near-symmetric lognormal centred at about $306 with monthly sigma ~13.4% (47%/3.5), with a slightly fatter left tail for a capex disappointment. This is essentially unchanged from round 1 (+1pp in the middle).

fair_value.method: Weights 50/30/20. P/E: FY28 core EPS $20.5 x 16x = $328. FCF yield: FY28 adj FCF $1.85B at 5.75% on ~102M shares = $315. Base-rate drift: JBL's median Sep-to-Sep 12-month price return since 2000 (+7%, n=26) applied to $304.41 = $326. Blend about $324.

I keep a discount to Flex because working capital is funded by +$8B of payables and GAAP EPS sits 26% below core. 16x sits between the 5-year average (~14x, TIKR) and today's 17.3x. The 5-year range is 4.7-9.3% (median ~6.8%), and the AI-era average is ~5.25%. 5.75% sits slightly above the AI-era level to reflect the working-capital intensity. bear.story: A hyperscaler capex digestion year in 2027, or a macro slowdown, stalls the cloud/data center ramp ($17.5B, +52% guided). JBL repeats its FY24 pattern (guide cut ~10%, FY27 ~$15.8), FY28 EPS stalls near $16.3, and the multiple falls to ~12x, the pre-AI norm, for ~$195. Base rate: JBL fell >20% in 3 of 26 Sep-Sep windows, and the two worst (2000-01 -68%, 2007-08 -58%) followed multi-year run-ups like the 2023-26 one. A ~20% weight is above the 12% unconditional rate because of AI concentration and 47% realized vol.

base.story: Jabil meets or slightly beats the FY27 guide (~$17.9 core EPS), as it has in 4 of the last 5 years. In late Sep-2027 it guides FY28 to ~$20.5 with growth slowing to the mid-teens, and the stock holds ~16x NTM, a discount to Flex's ~25x for working-capital-funded growth.

bull.story: 2027 hyperscaler capex again outruns consensus (as in 2024-25, when it grew >50% vs ~20% expected; Munster sees consensus rising from 23% toward 37%). JBL beats by a FY26-like +15-19%, FY28 EPS reaches ~$22.5, and the multiple moves to ~20x, closer to peers. That takes the stock to ~$460, above the June-2026 high of $429. Base rate: 35% of JBL's Sep-Sep years returned >30%, and 15% returned >50%.

thesis_break_reason: $211 is 12x the confirmed $17.55 FY27 guide, JBL's pre-AI multiple, and about 30% below spot. That is well below the ~$284-286 lows that held through the 2026 AI-hardware selloff and the post-print drop. Historically JBL has fallen >30% in a 12-month window only in genuine end-market busts (2000-01, 2007-08). Trading there would most likely mean the market is pricing a guide cut (cloud program loss or push-outs, a second-hyperscaler ramp slipping, or a working-capital squeeze) rather than ordinary volatility.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's established facts are the confirmed FY27 guide ($44.5B / 6.1% / $17.55 / ~$1.6B FCF), net debt of $1.64B, the segment mix (cloud +52%, networking +15%), Flex at ~25x, the FY25/FY26 guide beats of +13% and +19%, and the payables-funded working capital. Following the feedback for agent_5, I replaced the thin prediction-market inputs with base rates that fit the question. (1) Guide vs actual: JBL met or beat its initial full-year core EPS guide in 4 of the last 5 years (FY22 +20%, FY23 ~+2%, FY25 +13%, FY26 +19%) and missed once (FY24, ~-10% on a 13% revenue shortfall). The 12-month stock returns after those guides were -1%, +120%, -6%, +81% and +32%: even the miss year cost only -6% because buybacks and the multiple held. (2) Unconditional: across 26 Sep-to-Sep windows since 2000, JBL's median return is +7%, 54% of years are up, 12% are down >20%, 35% are up >30%, and the log SD is 0.41. Both crashes (-68%, -58%) came after multi-year run-ups and an end-market bust. (3) Valuation range: JBL's own FCF yield ran 4.7-9.3% over FY21-26 and compressed to 5.8% and 4.7% in the AI era, so my 6% was harsh; I now use 5.75%. Its pre-AI P/E of 8-13x is the wrong anchor for an asset mix that is now half AI, though working-capital intensity still justifies a discount to Flex. The result: FY28 EPS of $20.5 (from $20.2) at 16x (from 15.5x), and a fair value of $324 (from $309), which is close to the scenario-weighted value of ~$336 (with a mean above the median from the right skew). The ladder is a mixture: 88% lognormal with median ~$328 and sigma 0.37, plus 12% bust with median ~$200. I then blended it toward a single lognormal (median $320, sigma 0.40). That gives a median of ~$318, P(>=304) = 0.54, and a still-fat left tail (P(<213) = 17.5%) that exceeds the 8% unconditional rate of a >30% fall because of AI concentration and 47% realized vol. I disagree with the supervisor on one point: I keep the bull tail at P(>=533) = 9.5% rather than raising it further. Reaching it requires ~$22.5 EPS at ~24x, a peer multiple that JBL's working-capital-funded model has never held. Research limits: Twelve Data cash-flow statements and Alpha Vantage were unavailable (plan or rate limits), so FCF history comes from Jabil's own non-GAAP reconciliation PDF. The FY23 initial guide is approximate (from mid-year updates), and the FY24 initial EPS guide (~$9.45) is from memory corroborated by the 7% revenue cut, so it is labelled approximate.
